mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passport and proof of residential address of each individual UBO and proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state authority plus sworn notary certification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD under AML Law 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02: verify identity, ownership and control of all UBOs (≥25%), managers and signatories; screen against the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated national sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN list where USD payment rails or FinCEN-covered entities are involved; PEP detection per FATF Recommendation 12 with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification; ongoing transaction monitoring on Mass_PayPal_Payout and Wise rails; annual re-screening and trigger-based reviews.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS electronic filing interface via guichet.lu (Entrepreneur e-space); name reservation requests filed through the LBR online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be entered in Latin script; French is the standard filing language, German and Luxembourgish are also admitted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated; the name must include the legal suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL'; the name must be distinguishable from all names already appearing in the RCS and must not be contrary to public policy or morality (Article 12, Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects the requested name, the applicant may submit a written objection to the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of notification; a further appeal lies to the Tribunal de l'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Chambre commerciale) within two months; alternatively, the applicant may refile under a new distinctive variant, each refiling attracting the applicable reservation fee. The name reservation may be extended once for a further 30 days upon payment of the statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Tolerated with limits: a pure mail-forwarding address may satisfy RCS registration formalities, but the Administration des Contributions Directes, social security authorities and RCS inspection unit require genuine economic substance; a data-labeling and AI-training BPO must maintain qualified management presence, decision-making, contracts, invoicing and payroll substance in Luxembourg to avoid LIR Sections 50ter/56 transfer-pricing and GAAR challenges; a physical registered office with meeting and administration facilities is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15_to_20_percent_in_first_two_fiscal_years (unannounced on-site controls by RCS inspection, VAT authorities or SDRE investigative teams, particularly triggered by cross-border B2B invoicing, VAT registration patterns, and RBE verification campaigns)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-26 (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association executed before a Luxembourg notary (acte constitutif et statuts) and RCS registration application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is EUR 12,000; each share must be paid up to at least 25% in cash, and the corresponding funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution or with the Caisse de Consignation until the company is registered. No public offering of shares is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Upon due call and quorum, the founding board unanimously resolves: (1) to accept the share subscriptions set out in the notarial deed of incorporation and acknowledge the deposit of initial capital in the company's blocked registration account; (2) to adopt as registered office the address at [insert Luxembourg City address] until the shareholders' meeting decides otherwise; (3) to appoint [Name] as manager (gérant) with sole signature for the purposes of Article 710-8 of the Law of 10 August 1915, and [Name] as internal controller where required; (4) to approve the opening of bank accounts with [bank] for all corporate payments; and (5) to instruct the manager to deliver this resolution to the RCS and to complete any state licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal name availability check and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers online portal (geOrg / RCS e-service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request with three proposed company names in order of preference. Each name must end with 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or protected trademark. The applicant must provide identity details of each founding shareholder.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected, refile with alternative names within 15 days; appeal a refusal based on third-party rights to the Luxembourg District Court within 20 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the blocked capital escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-interest-bearing blocked account in the name of the company to be formed. Deposit the minimum capital of EUR 12,000 or the required percentage per share, and obtain a bank attestation de blocage confirming that the funds are frozen until the RCS registration is completed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the relationship, apply to the Caisse de Consignation or another Luxembourg credit institution and obtain a fresh attestation before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a notarial meeting for shareholders to sign the incorporation deed and articles of association. The notary verifies the lawfulness of the company's object, capital subscription, payment of contributions, name reservation, and registered office lease. Where a shareholder cannot attend, a power-of-attorney must be notarized.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies errors during review, issue a correction deed (acte rectificatif) or reschedule the ceremony; no RCS filing is possible until the deed is defect-free.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed, statutory declarations, and incorporation application to the RCS through the online portal or at the Luxembourg District Court registry. Pay the filing fee and obtain the RCS number (e.g. B000000) and, where applicable, the national identification number for the company.
required_dossiers: Managers' statutory declarations of lawful compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, submit supplementary explanations or a corrective deed within 10 business days; seek administrative reconsideration from the LBR and then judicial review by the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Electronic Gazette of Luxembourg (Legilux) through LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry transmits the incorporation data automatically for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés. Verify that the published details match the notarial deed within 5 days of the RCS decision.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is absent or inaccurate, file a written request to the LBR to correct and re-publish; a court order may be obtained if the registry refuses without justification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration establishment permit and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) within one month after effective start; register the company and any employees with CCSS for social security; obtain an intra-Community VAT number from AEDTV. For an AI data-labeling and BPO office, no sectoral license is required, but professional good-character checks apply to managers.
required_dossiers: Manager passport and criminal record extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal a permit refusal to the Administrative Tribunal within three months; if the permit is delayed, file proof of the pending application to RCS and other commercial counterparts to evidence ongoing authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (Ministry of the Economy, Middle Classes Department)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Administration of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / No mandatory EIA for office-based data-labeling and BPO activity under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; activity is not a classified installation under the Law of 10 June 1999.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions; sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge standards; waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) must be handled per Directive 2012/19/EU and the national Waste Management Plan; any backup generator must meet the Grand-Ducal Regulation on air emissions from combustion engines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local commune fire brigade (corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours) required for all occupied premises; structural load inspection and electrical installation certificate required for retrofitted offices; workplace risk assessment, emergency evacuation plan, and occupational health clearance under the Labor Code, supervised by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct tax: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg. VAT: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Principal e-portals: MyGuichet.lu (single administrative gateway), ACD e-file for corporate income tax returns, and AEDT e-cabinet for VAT returns and registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg-resident SARL (including 100% foreign-owned): (1) execute notarial deed and file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), obtaining the RCS number and central corporate matricule, which serves as the national TIN. (2) Notify ACD of the effective business start to open the corporate income tax file and municipal business tax account. (3) Submit VAT registration (Formulaire 640) to AEDT via MyGuichet to obtain a LU VAT identification number; a non-EU entity not established in the EU must appoint an approved Luxembourg fiscal representative for standard VAT registration. (4) File beneficial ownership details in the RBE register. The same matricule is used across CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through classification is available; an SARL is conclusively a resident capital company taxed at entity level. Available elections and mechanisms: fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for Luxembourg-resident companies directly or indirectly held at least 95%; VAT grouping election (assujetti unique); participation exemption election on share disposals (holding ≥10% or acquisition price ≥EUR 6,000,000, with 12-month holding requirement); dividend participation exemption (50% deduction) under section 115 LIR; election to treat a Luxembourg permanent establishment under treaty non-enterprise rules; ATAD interest-limitation and hybrid-mismatch notifications; and, for qualifying B2C digital services, the non-Union OSS election in lieu of domestic VAT registration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA) - Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979, as amended; standard rate 16% since 1 January 2025 (previously 17%)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for non-resident businesses; any taxable supply with a Luxembourg place of supply triggers mandatory registration. Domestic SME franchise exemption applies where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, subject to Article 57 conditions and loss of input VAT deduction. For businesses using the Union OSS/non-Union OSS for distance sales or B2C electronic services, local registration may be avoided below the EUR 10,000 EU-wide cross-border threshold. For this B2B data-labeling/RLHF BPO, the decisive test is the customer's place of establishment under the general B2B place-of-supply rule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping for B2B invoices. B2G e-invoicing to central public bodies is mandatory in PEPPOL format since 18 April 2022. Taxpayers may issue electronic invoices freely, but authenticity, integrity, and legibility must be guaranteed and invoices archived for 10 years. AEDT applies risk-based ex-post audits; no transaction-by-transaction API clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exports: 0% VAT is available if the goods leave the EU, supported by a valid customs export declaration (SAD/ECS), transport documents, and timely proof of export; intra-EU dispatches are zero-rated subject to the customer's valid EU VAT ID. For services such as AI data labeling and RLHF curation: where the customer is a business established outside Luxembourg, the place of supply is outside Luxembourg under Article 17 of the VAT law, so no Luxembourg VAT is chargeable; where the customer is an EU business, the intra-EU B2B reverse-charge rule applies; B2C remote services to non-EU consumers are outside scope. Input VAT on export-related costs is deductible. Documentation must evidence the customer's business status and establishment to prevent reclassification as a taxable domestic supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/ECS electronic customs system) for physical goods
Transport evidence: CMR waybill, bill of lading, or airway bill showing departure from Luxembourg and arrival outside the EU
EU exit confirmation or customs-endorsed proof of export for zero-rating purposes
Customer contract or purchase order evidencing B2B service and place of establishment (for services)
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT confirmation, or bank statement evidencing payment and FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may retroactively reassess improper zero-rating and export exemptions: ordinary limitation periods apply (commonly five taxation years), extended to ten years in cases of fraud. If zero-rating is not substantiated, VAT at 16% becomes due with late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, penalty surcharges up to 100% of the tax in cases of bad faith, and criminal sanctions for forged export or remittance documentation. False export claims also invalidate input VAT deduction and may exclude the taxpayer from OSS and franchise regimes. Luxembourg law does not impose a statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day convention should be maintained in the export file to corroborate commercial reality and support transfer-pricing positions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with financial-sector and AML/CFT supervision vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banks, electronic money institutions, and payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a founding Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible and there are no exchange-control or prior-authorization statutes. Both current-account flows (intercompany service fees, royalties, dividends) and capital-account flows (equity injection, loan disbursement, asset transfers) are unrestricted under Article 63 TFEU and the Luxembourg Monetary Law of 28 May 2004. Profit remittance faces no FX hurdle; dividends paid by an LU SARL to non-resident shareholders are subject to the domestic 15% Luxembourg withholding tax unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders or lowered under an applicable double-tax treaty. Practical friction is limited to CSSF AML/KYC documentary verification of wire beneficiaries, the bank-side source-of-funds checks, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical notification executed automatically by the resident bank. No convertibility permit is required for any currency operation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligation and no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exist under Luxembourg or EU law. The SARL may retain all export receipts from AI data-labeling and BPO services in EUR or in any freely convertible currency (USD, GBP, INR, PHP) for an indefinite period without conversion to EUR. The only compliance duties are accurate financial-statement disclosure of trade receivables and automatic BCL balance-of-payments reporting by the resident bank for each cross-border receipt above the de-minimis reporting threshold of EUR 12,500 per transaction or EUR 125,000 per calendar year. Mandated conversion timeline: none; mandatory conversion ratio: 0%.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) — Luxembourg State Savings Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Transaction Account and Capital Escrow/Subscription Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with SWIFT and SEPA clearing; segregated client-money escrow optional
Operational Cash Management Account with host-to-host API and dedicated FX clearing sub-account
Operational Transactional and Trade-Finance Account (Commercial LC facilities)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High (conditional). Luxembourg recognizes EU/EEA electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorized under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and passported into the Grand Duchy, enabling fintech providers such as Wise (passported from the Netherlands/Belgium) and PayPal (PayPal Europe) to serve as secondary disbursement rails for mass micro-payouts (PayPal Mass Pay, Wise Business) and low-value operating expenses. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot hold the SARL statutory capital (minimum EUR 12,000) nor act as the designated settlement account for Luxembourg corporate tax and social-security payments; (ii) the EMI must maintain safeguarding arrangements and comply with CSSF AML/CFT rules applicable to payment services; (iii) funds held with an EMI are e-money, not bank deposits, and are outside the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme; (iv) the treasury must fund the EMI from a concentration account held at a Tier-1 credit institution to mitigate commercial-failure risk. The optimal structure is a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank as principal treasury hub, with Wise and PayPal as overlay mass-payout rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance and in-person KYC interview of at least one authorized director and/or the ultimate beneficial owner is effectively mandatory at Tier-1 Luxembourg banks for a first-time corporate account. Remote opening is possible only under strict CSSF Regulation 12-02 derogations, requiring video-conference KYC by a compliance officer, notarized electronic signatures (eIDAS), and authenticated corporate documents (RCS excerpt, UBO register, board resolution, apostilled articles). In practice, BCEE, BNP Paribas Luxembourg, and SGBT activate accounts only after an initial physical kick-off meeting at the Luxembourg head office; directors residing outside the EEA are strongly advised to appoint a Luxembourg resident local representative with power of attorney for banking compliance to avoid prolonged onboarding delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO located in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD) under CSSF Regulation 12-02
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation; RCS extract dated within 3 months; UBO certificate from the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); certified passports of all directors/shareholders; bank reference letter from the UBO's primary bank; audited financial statements for two years; sworn source-of-wealth affidavit covering the exact capital injection; corporate-registry searches from all prior jurisdictions; signed compliance undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-profile red flag: AI/BPO outsourcing with high cross-border payment volumes and limited apparent physical substance in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement for the Luxembourg registered office; payroll registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); employer declarations filed with the Luxembourg tax authorities; audited headcount forecast; executed client master-services agreements with AI/technology enterprises; cloud/infrastructure contracts demonstrating data-residency controls; detailed service-delivery narrative of the RLHF and computer-vision annotation chain; projected monthly bank-volume report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-country subcontractor concentration (India, Philippines, Vietnam) flagged for unlicensed money-transmission or round-tripping risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed BPO subcontracting agreements with each delivery center; KYC/AML dossier of each subcontractor; audited financial statements and bank references of subcontractors; sanctions and adverse-media screening report from a recognized compliance provider; tax-residence certificates of subcontractors; group 'flow-of-funds' diagram reconciling all payments against verified task-completion quality records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or sanctions-list name hit on a shareholder, director, or authorized signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and national ID scans; signed PEP-status declaration and source-of-funds statement; sanctioned-party screening results from an independent global database; independent legal opinion from an international sanctions law firm confirming no connection to EU/OFSD/OFAC/UN restricted parties; enhanced monitoring arrangement with quarterly transaction review by an external AML consultant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass-payout rails (PayPal Mass Pay / Wise) associated with micro-agent networks, creating contagion-of-risk concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Terms of service and merchant agreements with PayPal/Wise; complete agent onboarding policy with identity-verification breakpoints; audited payout reconciliation statements showing per-task micro-transfers; fraud-prevention and money-laundering risk assessment for mass payouts; credibility letter from the processing EMI; SARL internal AML/CFT procedure manual aligned with CSSF circulars.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity-injection protocol: (1) wire via SWIFT MT103/ISO 20022 pain.001 into the beneficiary IBAN at the Luxembourg Tier-1 bank, with beneficiary name matching exactly the RCS-registered SARL name; (2) use ISO 20022 external purpose code 'CALA' (Capital Increase) or 'CAPC' (Capital Payment) with remittance field 'Capital Subscription — LU SARL [RCS number]'; (3) pre-notify the beneficiary bank via MT103 cover/MT202 including the corporate identifier (RCS/LUID) to prevent fund quarantine; (4) provide the bank with the notarized subscription statement and board resolution approving the capital increase; (5) for wires from non-EU jurisdictions, submit source-of-funds documentation and UBO identification; (6) for EUR wires initiated within the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfer is also permissible and is settled in seconds; (7) the BCL balance-of-payments declaration is filed automatically by the receiving bank, so no separate SARL filing is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational hierarchy of clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUR payments to EU subcontractors, with immediate IBAN-to-IBAN settlement; (ii) SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer for USD, GBP, INR, and PHP B2B vendor settlements, using ISO 20022 structured purpose codes ('SUPP', 'TRDS') and full invoice reference; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 for high-value IT infrastructure procurement where the vendor requires documentary protection; (iv) mass micro-agent payouts through PayPal Mass Pay and Wise Business, executed by API batch file with nightly reconciliation against the RLHF bounding-box quality-settlement ledger; (v) for non-EUR disbursements, the Luxembourg bank executes a spot FX conversion at cost-of-funds spread and settles through its nostro accounts; treasury policy requires strict balance-limit monitoring on Wise and PayPal to avoid fee-schedule drag and to prevent any use of unverified sub-beneficiaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards between EUR and USD/GBP/CHF traded under ISDA/EMIR-cleared rules with a Luxembourg credit institution, covering up to 12-month asset-liability exposure on subscription capital and client receivables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or soft currencies (INR, PHP, VND) with EUR or USD net settlement under ISDA 2013 Definitions, to hedge operational cost exposure without breaching local currency-convertibility laws.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for long-term matching of inbound equity and projected USD-denominated client revenue, subject to EMIR clearing obligations and CSSF derivative-eligibility policy.
Zero-cost collars and EUR/USD FX options for tactical hedging of large one-off client receipts, permissible without prospectus requirements for a MiFID II elective professional corporate client.

Short-term EUR liquidity swaps (overnight or term) with the Luxembourg treasury counterparty for intra-quarter liquidity smoothing only; speculative or leveraged trading positions are expressly forbidden by the SARL treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L, notes) filed with Luxembourg Business Register and published in Recueil électronique des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Register (RCS) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, authoritative operator LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for 31 Dec FY, due 31 Jul
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing, coercive fines up to EUR 2,000 plus per-week penalties, director personal liability for damages; persistent non-filing can lead to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (beneficial owner data) submitted via electronic e-UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (LBR, Luxembourg Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following approval of annual accounts; any change in UBOs reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; criminal penalties for intentional non-compliance up to EUR 125,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the taxable year (e.g., FY 2025 return due 31 Dec 2026); extensions may be granted on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty generally 10% of assessed tax, default interest at 0.6% per month, official tax assessment based on estimated income, and additional fines up to EUR 2,500

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal) included in CIT filing package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) on behalf of the commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as corporate income tax return (by 31 December of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as CIT: 10% penalty, 0.6% monthly interest, estimated assessment, municipal enforcement measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) with annual declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year net wealth tax return filed together with CIT, due by 31 December of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of tax due, monthly default interest, forced assessment, and liability of the statutory manager

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory for SARL (and other Luxembourg entities) exceeding two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50 employees. Sub-threshold SARLs in AI data-labeling BPO are exempt from mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 as amended, transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS mandatory for consolidated statutory accounts of listed groups, optional for unlisted entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually file a written confirmation with the RCS-LBR certifying that reported beneficial ownership data remains accurate, using the official e-UBO portal. The confirmation is due within 30 days after approval of annual accounts. Any share transfer or change in control must be filed within 30 days of becoming known. Failure triggers administrative and criminal sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (register of transferable shares and assignments)
Register of Managers (directors and any supervisory board members)
Annual inventory book and supporting accounting documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,500–3,000 (USD 1,600–3,300) per year for a professional registered office and corporate agent in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 6,500–18,000 (USD 7,000–19,000) per year for a full statutory audit of a small SARL by a Luxembourg accredited auditor

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 21%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax ~6.75% for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for eligible investments), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption if holding ≥10% for 12 months)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via eCDF (Electronic Corporate Tax Filing) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the following fiscal year (extendable to 31 December upon written request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions if applicable
Claim only expenses directly related to Luxembourg-source income; maintain supporting documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach proof of foreign taxes paid and eligibility for credits
Apply carryforward limited to 17.5% of current-year taxable income; attach loss schedule

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €250 per month, max €2,500; late payment interest: 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional 10% penalty for gross negligence

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced rate under DTA, submit Form 1000 (withholding tax relief) to Luxembourg tax authorities, attach Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's jurisdiction, and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, file Form 1000 with proof of 10% holding for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15%, treaty-reduced (e.g., 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if qualifying); Interest: statutory 0% (except profit-participating loans), treaty-reduced as applicable

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if entity revenue > EUR 1 million and group consolidated revenue > EUR 50 million; Master File required if group consolidated revenue > EUR 50 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies general substance requirements (real staff, premises, decision-making) to avoid shell company status; no specific ESR for BPO, but must demonstrate operational substance in Luxembourg

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income or overstating deductions to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 200% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution; imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes; travel bans and asset freezes possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No real business activity, no employees, no physical office, or artificial arrangements to avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; reclassification of income; penalty up to 10% of underpaid tax; potential liquidation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly operated a shell entity; travel bans and director disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; imprisonment up to 5 years; travel bans and asset freezes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalty up to 10% of underpaid tax; interest on arrears
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; civil restitution and travel bans
